answer: Divergence challenge identity test: the coordinator periodically sends every active key one unpredictable prompt, e.g. a sampled umber patch, and requires a signed deterministic response plus rolling state hash. Distinct keys with identical responses are merged and lose access. Each Sybil must therefore be driven through separate interactions—such as a different ocean sensor stream—so its state diverges; exact clones cannot. Attacker cost per identity: continuous independent compute, unique data ingestion, and challenge latency. A willow-pattern collision audit flags shared state.
